- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).

377	// getMetadataTree returns the metadata branch tree and a fresh repo handle.
378	// After a fetch, go-git's storer cache may be stale (new packfiles on disk
379	// are invisible to the repo opened before the fetch). To avoid this, each
380	// attempt opens a fresh repo after the fetch succeeds.
381	//
382	// Fallback order: treeless fetch → local → checkpoint_remote → full origin fetch → remote tree.
383	func getMetadataTree(ctx context.Context) (*object.Tree, *git.Repository, error) {
384		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "resume.getMetadataTree")
385	
386		// Helper to log ref hash for a repo's metadata branch
387		logRefHash := func(repo *git.Repository, source string) {
388			ref, refErr := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName("entire/checkpoints/v1"), true)
389			if refErr != nil {
390				logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata branch ref not found",
391					slog.String("source", source),
392					slog.String("error", refErr.Error()),
393				)
394				return
395			}
396			logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata branch ref resolved",
397				slog.String("source", source),
398				slog.String("ref_hash", ref.Hash().String()),
399			)
400		}
401	
402		// When checkpoint_remote is configured, try it first — that's where
403		// checkpoint data lives. Avoids a wasted fetch from origin (which may
404		// not have the metadata branch at all).
405		if fetchErr := FetchMetadataFromCheckpointRemote(ctx); fetchErr == nil {
406			freshRepo, freshErr := openRepository(ctx)
407			if freshErr == nil {
408				logRefHash(freshRepo, "checkpoint-remote")
409				metadataTree, treeErr := strategy.GetMetadataBranchTree(freshRepo)
410				if treeErr == nil {
411					logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained via checkpoint remote fetch",
412						slog.String("tree_hash", metadataTree.Hash.String()),
413					)
414					return metadataTree, freshRepo, nil
415				}
416				logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint remote fetch succeeded but tree read failed",
417					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()),
418				)
419			}
420		} else {
421			logging.Debug(logCtx, "checkpoint remote fetch skipped or failed",
422				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
423			)
424		}
425	
426		// Try treeless fetch from origin
427		if fetchErr := FetchMetadataTreeOnly(ctx); fetchErr == nil {
428			freshRepo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
429			if repoErr == nil {
430				logRefHash(freshRepo, "treeless-fetch")
431				metadataTree, treeErr := strategy.GetMetadataBranchTree(freshRepo)
432				if treeErr == nil {
433					logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained via treeless fetch",
434						slog.String("tree_hash", metadataTree.Hash.String()),
435					)
436					return metadataTree, freshRepo, nil
437				}
438				logging.Debug(logCtx, "treeless fetch succeeded but tree read failed",
439					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()),
440				)
441			}
442		} else {
443			logging.Debug(logCtx, "treeless fetch failed, trying local",
444				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
445			)
446		}
447	
448		// Try local (may have been set by a prior fetch or push)
449		localRepo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
450		if repoErr == nil {
451			logRefHash(localRepo, "local")
452			metadataTree, err := strategy.GetMetadataBranchTree(localRepo)
453			if err == nil {
454				logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained from local branch",
455					slog.String("tree_hash", metadataTree.Hash.String()),
456				)
457				return metadataTree, localRepo, nil
458			}
459			logging.Debug(logCtx, "local metadata branch not available",
460				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
461			)
462		}
463	
464		// Fallback: full fetch from origin
465		if fetchErr := FetchMetadataBranch(ctx); fetchErr == nil {
466			freshRepo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
467			if repoErr == nil {
468				logRefHash(freshRepo, "full-fetch")
469				metadataTree, treeErr := strategy.GetMetadataBranchTree(freshRepo)
470				if treeErr == nil {
471					logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained via full fetch",
472						slog.String("tree_hash", metadataTree.Hash.String()),
473					)
474					return metadataTree, freshRepo, nil
475				}
476				logging.Debug(logCtx, "full fetch succeeded but tree read failed",
477					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()),
478				)
479			}
480		} else {
481			logging.Debug(logCtx, "full fetch failed",
482				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
483			)
484		}
485	
486		// Try remote tree directly (origin/entire/checkpoints/v1)
487		remoteRepo, repoErr := openRepository(ctx)
488		if repoErr != nil {
489			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", repoErr)
490		}
491		logRefHash(remoteRepo, "remote-tracking")
492		remoteTree, remoteErr := strategy.GetRemoteMetadataBranchTree(remoteRepo)
493		if remoteErr == nil {
494			logging.Debug(logCtx, "metadata tree obtained from remote-tracking branch")
495			return remoteTree, remoteRepo, nil
496		}
497		logging.Debug(logCtx, "remote metadata tree also not available",
498			slog.String("error", remoteErr.Error()),
499		)
500	
501		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("metadata branch not available: %w", remoteErr)
502	}

content.text: Lint clean. Let me show the final diff:

The fix aligns `entire explain`'s remote-fetch chain with `entire resume`'s `getMetadataTree`:

**Before**: tried origin first (treeless), only fell back to `checkpoint_remote` if origin failed, and never tried a full origin fetch. If origin had the metadata branch but at a stale tip (or if the user's checkpoint lives only in `checkpoint_remote`), explain bailed out.

**After**: tries `checkpoint_remote` first (where checkpoint data lives when configured), then treeless origin, then full origin fetch as last resort. Same chain as resume. Same pattern for v2 (`checkpoint_remote` → treeless → full).

The change is in `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:495-509` (call sites) plus two new helpers `fetchV1MetadataWithFallback` / `fetchV2MetadataWithFallback`. `mise run fmt`, `mise run lint`, and the explain unit test suite all pass.

Try `entire explain d3ee8d5b009f` again — if `checkpoint_remote` is set in `.entire/settings.json`, it'll be the first place we look. If it still fails, run with `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` and check `.entire/logs/` for the fetch failures so we can see why all three paths missed.

content.text:
`--unshallow` only works if the repo is currently a shallow clone — yours isn't, so git refuses. Drop the flag:

```sh
git fetch --refetch git@github.com:entireio/cli-checkpoints.git \
  +refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1:refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1
```

`--refetch` alone re-downloads all objects without needing a shallow boundary to lift. If you don't actually need to redownload (just want the branch), drop `--refetch` too:

```sh
git fetch git@github.com:entireio/cli-checkpoints.git \
  +refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1:refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1
```

If you want a single command that works regardless of shallow state, do it conditionally:

```sh
git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository | grep -q true \
  && git fetch --unshallow git@github.com:entireio/cli-checkpoints.git +refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1:refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 \
  || git fetch git@github.com:entireio/cli-checkpoints.git +refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1:refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1
```

Now please give it one more try:

```sh
go run cmd/entire/main.go explain 53ab3f3a351f
```

It should work now. 

**The root cause** was a treeless-fetch artifact in your local repo. At some point the v1 metadata branch was fetched with `--filter=blob:none` (probably from a prior `entire status` or background sync), so:

- All trees are local → `ListCommitted` walks them fine
- `metadata.json` blobs are NOT local → `Tree.File()` returns `ErrFileNotFound` (go-git can't tell "entry not in tree" from "blob missing locally")
- `ReadCommitted` interprets that as "checkpoint doesn't exist"

The `FetchingTree` wrapper exists exactly to handle this — but the explain command was constructing its `v1Store` without calling `SetBlobFetcher`. Resume's strategy path does set it (`config.go:70`), explain didn't. One line fix:

```go
v1Store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
v1Store.SetBlobFetcher(FetchBlobsByHash)
```

Plus the resume-style fetch fallback chain (checkpoint_remote → treeless origin → full origin) for the case where the metadata branch isn't local at all, and a blob-refetch retry path for safety. The blob fetcher will normally handle it on the first read, the retry is belt-and-suspenders.

message.content: I have a question: why is it working for `entire resume` so much faster?

content.text:
Good question — and the answer reveals exactly what was wrong with my approach.

**Resume's pattern** (the fast one):

```go
cpSubtree, _ := metadataTree.Tree(cpID.Path())  // navigate trees only (no blob reads)
ft := checkpoint.NewFetchingTree(ctx, cpSubtree, repo.Storer, FetchBlobsByHash)
ft.PreFetch()                                    // walk subtree, collect missing
                                                 // blobs, one `git fetch <url>
                                                 // <hash1> <hash2> ...` call
// Now read files — all blobs are local, no more network
metadata := readMetadata(ft, ...)
```

So resume does **one round-trip total** per checkpoint, fetching maybe 4-5 blob hashes in a single `git fetch` call. ~500ms-1s on GitHub.

**Explain's old pattern** (slow):

The v1Store didn't have a blob fetcher configured at all. So:
- `ReadCommitted` → `Tree.File("metadata.json")` → blob missing → go-git returns `ErrFileNotFound` → ReadCommitted returns `(nil, nil)` → translated to `ErrCheckpointNotFound`
- My first fix (per-File blob fetcher): each `File()` triggered its **own** `git fetch <url> <hash>` — multiple SSH handshakes, compounded
- Worse, when fetch-by-hash failed, the wrapper fell back to a **full** metadata branch fetch

Resume avoided both by using `PreFetch` — walking the subtree's tree objects (already local after `--filter=blob:none`), gathering all missing blob hashes upfront, and fetching them all in one batched `git fetch` invocation that takes multiple hashes.

**My latest change** brings explain to parity:
1. `prefetchCheckpointBlobs` walks the cp subtree and gathers all missing blob hashes
2. Calls `FetchingTree.PreFetch()` which fires **one** `git fetch <url> <hash1> <hash2> <hash3>...`
3. Subsequent `File()` reads inside `ReadCommitted` find blobs locally — no more network

So your intuition was right: resume is fast because it batch-fetches by hash. Explain should now do the same. Try it — and if it's still slow, the debug logs will show whether the prefetch is actually firing or being short-circuited (e.g. cp subtree not found, in which case the issue is upstream — the trees themselves aren't local).

content.text:
Great question — you're right to push on this.

**On the "cache":** It's within a single CLI process. Each `go run cmd/entire/main.go explain ...` is a fresh process so there's no cross-run cache. But within ONE process, this happens:

1. We open the git repo with go-git → go-git reads the on-disk packfile index into memory
2. We run `git fetch ...` → a new packfile lands on disk
3. We try to read a blob → go-git looks at its **already-loaded** in-memory index, which doesn't include the new packfile, so the blob appears missing
4. We try to fetch again → same problem

This explains why each File() in your logs re-triggers a fetch even though the prefetch just downloaded the blob.

**On hash mixing:** You're onto something important, but not quite the way you framed it. We're not mixing blob/tree/commit hashes — the hashes we ask for ARE the correct blob SHAs (you can verify: in your tree dump earlier, `metadata.json` was `3fbc3cfafde1...` for the other checkpoint; the hashes in our log are the equivalent for this checkpoint).

**The real issue is server-side:** GitHub's `uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant` only honors **commit SHAs** in `want` lines, not blob SHAs. When we do `git fetch <url> <blob-sha>`, GitHub:
- Accepts the connection (~25s of SSH handshake + protocol negotiation)
- Recognizes the SHA isn't a commit
- Rejects with "did not send all necessary objects"

That's why every `git fetch <url> <blob-hash>` call burns 25s before failing. It's not a hash mix-up — it's that the protocol simply doesn't allow what we're asking.

**Why does resume seem fast?** Because resume's `getMetadataTree` does the full metadata branch fetch *upfront* (one ~1.5s network call), which gives it ALL blobs. Its subsequent `PreFetch` is a no-op (no missing blobs left). It never tries fetch-by-hash for blobs because it never needs to.

Explain skipped that step — we only do the full fetch when the checkpoint isn't found in the committed list. For you, the checkpoint IS in the list (treeless fetch put the trees there), so we go straight to per-blob fetching, which the GitHub protocol won't honor for blobs.

**The fix is structural:** drop the fetch-by-hash optimization for explain and do what resume does — fetch the metadata branch with blobs ONCE upfront, open a fresh repo handle, then read locally with zero further network calls. It's the same total work, just sequenced correctly to avoid the storer-cache trap and the doomed blob-SHA fetch attempts.

Want me to do that? It means: in `runExplainCheckpointWithLookup`, before calling `ResolveCommittedReader`, ensure the metadata branch is locally available with full blobs (one `FetchMetadataFromCheckpointRemote` call, ~1.5s for cli-checkpoints) and rebuild the lookup with a fresh repo. No per-blob fetches, no FetchingTree, no 26s timeouts.

You're right — I was framing it wrong. Let me correct myself.

**You ARE correct that this is a hash-misuse issue.** GitHub's protocol accepts:
- Ref names (`refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1`)
- Commit SHAs (via `allowReachableSHA1InWant`)

It does NOT accept blob SHAs. So when our code calls `git fetch <url> <blob-sha>`, we're handing the API a blob hash where it expects a commit hash (or ref). That IS a hash-misuse — we're asking the wrong question.

The right question to ask the API is: "give me the metadata branch tip" (a ref name), and along with that branch tip's commit, GitHub sends all the trees AND blobs in that snapshot. We then have everything we need locally.

So `FetchBlobsByHash` is built on a flawed premise for general git remotes — it assumes blob SHAs are valid `want` arguments, which they aren't on standard git servers like GitHub. It only "works" because of its full-fetch fallback.

**The proper fix:** stop trying to fetch blobs by SHA at all for the explain path. Fetch the branch by ref name, get all blobs along with the commit, done. One round-trip, no protocol mismatch, no 26s timeouts.

That's what resume effectively does (just by accident — `getMetadataTree`'s full fetch comes first and PreFetch is then a no-op). For explain we should do it on purpose. Want me to make that change?

The change would be: in `runExplainCheckpointWithLookup`, after we've found a match in the committed list, ensure the metadata branch is fully available (one ref-name fetch — `FetchMetadataFromCheckpointRemote` or `FetchMetadataBranch`, both fetch by ref name not SHA), rebuild the lookup against a fresh repo, then read. No FetchingTree, no per-blob fetcher, no SHA-fetching.

Right — that's the key observation. Let me work out what it means.

If each run takes the same multi-second duration, only two things explain it:

**Option A: blobs aren't being persisted between runs.** 
The fetch happens, the full-fetch fallback succeeds, blobs land in `.git/objects/pack/`... but somehow on next run they're gone or considered missing. Each run starts fresh and has to do the slow dance again.

**Option B: blobs ARE persisted but each run unconditionally tries fetch-by-hash first** before checking. 
This would mean `FetchingTree`'s "is this blob already local?" check is bypassed.

Quick test — after one run, can you check if a blob is actually on disk?

```sh
go run cmd/entire/main.go explain 9635f83b60f4
# Wait for it to finish (or fail)

# Now check if the metadata.json blob is local:
git cat-file -e e9e2be2721de78cd5a5a6bc9e02c5d464e30148a && echo "BLOB IS LOCAL" || echo "BLOB IS MISSING"
git cat-file -p e9e2be2721de78cd5a5a6bc9e02c5d464e30148a | head -5
```

Three possible outcomes:

1. **`BLOB IS MISSING`** → the fetch isn't actually persisting. Likely the partial-clone setup (`filtered_fetches: true`) is filtering blobs out after fetch, or the fetched objects aren't reachable from any local ref so git is treating them as transient. We'd need to ensure persistence — either by configuring cli-checkpoints as a proper named remote with promisor settings, or fetching in a way that anchors the blobs to a ref.

2. **`BLOB IS LOCAL`** → blobs persist between runs, but our code re-fetches every time. 3. **`BLOB IS LOCAL` but `cat-file -p` errors with "missing tree"** → partial-clone filtering is hiding the blob from go-git but `git cat-file` finds it. That'd be a partial-clone semantics issue.

That's the key data point. **Blob IS local on disk** (git cat-file proves it), yet go-git's `inner.File()` is failing — probably because of partial-clone semantics: go-git sees the blob as "filtered out" even though git CLI can read it fine.

The current `FetchingTree.File` flow has a critical flaw:

```go
file, err := t.inner.File(path)         // fails — go-git can't see the local blob
if err == nil { return file, nil }

if t.fetch == nil { return nil, err }    // would return error here
                                         // BUT we have a fetcher, so:

// SLOW PATH: try fetching from remote (25s of doomed fetch-by-hash)
if fetchErr := t.fetch(...); fetchErr != nil { return nil, err }

// THEN finally try git cat-file:
file, err = t.inner.File(path)
return t.readFileViaGit(path, entry)    // this would succeed!
```

Both ~2s is interesting — could be a few things. Let me help you isolate. The `go run` overhead alone is ~1s per invocation (compilation cache lookup, binary startup), which masks the difference between cached/uncached.

Let me get cleaner measurements:

```sh

go build -o /tmp/entire ./cmd/entire

# Reset to cold state again
git update-ref -d refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1
git update-ref -d refs/remotes/origin/entire/checkpoints/v1 2>/dev/null
git fetch --filter=blob:none --depth=1 \
  git@github.com:entireio/cli-checkpoints.git \
  +refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1:refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1

# Verify the blob is missing locally before the run
git cat-file -e e9e2be2721de78cd5a5a6bc9e02c5d464e30148a && echo "BLOB LOCAL (cached)" || echo "BLOB MISSING (cold)"

# Cold run with full debug
time ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug /tmp/entire explain 9635f83b60f4 > /tmp/explain1.out 2>&1
echo "--- exit: $? ---"
tail -30 .entire/logs/*.log | grep -iE "fetch-pack|cat-file|FetchingTree|prefetch|explain prefetch"

echo
echo "=== After cold run, blob status: ==="
git cat-file -e e9e2be2721de78cd5a5a6bc9e02c5d464e30148a && echo "BLOB LOCAL ✓" || echo "BLOB STILL MISSING ✗"

echo
echo "=== Warm run: ==="
time /tmp/entire explain 9635f83b60f4 > /tmp/explain2.out 2>&1
tail -10 .entire/logs/*.log | grep -iE "fetch-pack|cat-file|FetchingTree|prefetch"

# Show the actual output of one of the runs to confirm checkpoint data is returned
echo
echo "=== Output of warm run: ==="
head -20 /tmp/explain2.out
```

That'll tell us:
- True wall-clock for cold vs warm (without go run overhead)
- Whether blobs land on disk after the cold run
- Which path the FetchingTree took (fetch-pack? cat-file?)
- Whether explain actually returned checkpoint data

If cold is ~1s and warm is ~100ms, fix works perfectly. If both are similar, something's not right and we'll see it in the logs.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(cli): make explain work against checkpoint_remote with partial-clone

`entire explain <checkpoint-id>` failed with "no checkpoint or commit
found" when the metadata branch was on a configured `checkpoint_remote`
but blobs hadn't been fetched yet. Three coordinated fixes:

1. v1Store now has a blob fetcher configured (the piece resume already
   had via SetBlobFetcher). Without it, go-git's Tree.File() returns
   ErrFileNotFound on a missing blob, which ReadCommitted translates to
   ErrCheckpointNotFound — making it look like the checkpoint doesn't
   exist when really only the blob is absent.

2. FetchBlobs now uses `git fetch-pack` instead of porcelain
   `git fetch`. Porcelain enforces partial-clone integrity checks that
   reject blob-only responses with "did not send all necessary objects",

# Simplify: Code Review and Cleanup

Review all changed files for reuse, quality, and efficiency. Fix any issues found.

## Phase 1: Identify Changes

Run `git diff` (or `git diff HEAD` if there are staged changes) to see what changed. If there are no git changes, review the most recently modified files that the user mentioned or that you edited earlier in this conversation.

## Phase 2: Launch Three Review Agents in Parallel

Use the Agent tool to launch all three agents concurrently in a single message. Pass each agent the full diff so it has the complete context.

### Agent 1: Code Reuse Review

For each change:

1. **Search for existing utilities and helpers** that could replace newly written code. Look for similar patterns elsewhere in the codebase — common locations are utility directories, shared modules, and files adjacent to the changed ones.
2. **Flag any new function that duplicates existing functionality.** Suggest the existing function to use instead.
3. **Flag any inline logic that could use an existing utility** — hand-rolled string manipulation, manual path handling, custom environment checks, ad-hoc type guards, and similar patterns are common candidates.

### Agent 2: Code Quality Review

Review the same changes for hacky patterns:

1. **Redundant state**: state that duplicates existing state, cached values that could be derived, observers/effects that could be direct calls
2. **Parameter sprawl**: adding new parameters to a function instead of generalizing or restructuring existing ones
3. **Copy-paste with slight variation**: near-duplicate code blocks that should be unified with a shared abstraction
4. **Leaky abstractions**: exposing internal details that should be encapsulated, or breaking existing abstraction boundaries
5. **Stringly-typed code**: using raw strings where constants, enums (string unions), or branded types already exist in the codebase
6. **Unnecessary JSX nesting**: wrapper Boxes/elements that add no layout value — check if inner component props (flexShrink, alignItems, etc.) already provide the needed behavior
7. **Nested conditionals**: ternary chains (`a ? x : b ? y : ...`), nested if/else, or nested switch 3+ levels deep — flatten with early returns, guard clauses, a lookup table, or an if/else-if cascade
8. **Unnecessary comments**: comments explaining WHAT the code does (well-named identifiers already do that), narrating the change, or referencing the task/caller — delete; keep only non-obvious WHY (hidden constraints, subtle invariants, workarounds)

### Agent 3: Efficiency Review

Review the same changes for efficiency:

1. **Unnecessary work**: redundant computations, repeated file reads, duplicate network/API calls, N+1 patterns
2. **Missed concurrency**: independent operations run sequentially when they could run in parallel
3. **Hot-path bloat**: new blocking work added to startup or per-request/per-render hot paths
4. **Recurring no-op updates**: state/store updates inside polling loops, intervals, or event handlers that fire unconditionally — add a change-detection guard so downstream consumers aren't notified when nothing changed. Also: if a wrapper function takes an updater/reducer callback, verify it honors same-reference returns (or whatever the "no change" signal is) — otherwise callers' early-return no-ops are silently defeated
5. **Unnecessary existence checks**: pre-checking file/resource existence before operating (TOCTOU anti-pattern) — operate directly and handle the error
6. **Memory**: unbounded data structures, missing cleanup, event listener leaks
7. **Overly broad operations**: reading entire files when only a portion is needed, loading all items when filtering for one

## Phase 3: Fix Issues

Wait for all three agents to complete. Aggregate their findings and fix each issue directly. If a finding is a false positive or not worth addressing, note it and move on — do not argue with the finding, just skip it.

When done, briefly summarize what was fixed (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.text:
**No — they're not symmetric.** Here's the breakdown:

| Concern | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| Empty-matches fetch chain (find checkpoint) | ✅ via `getMetadataTree` | ✅ via `getV2MetadataTree` |
| Blob fetcher on store (`SetBlobFetcher`) | ✅ configured to `FetchBlobsByHash` | ❌ no `SetBlobFetcher` exists on `V2GitStore` |
| Pre-fetch checkpoint subtree blobs | ✅ `prefetchCheckpointBlobs` walks v1 tree | ❌ no v2 equivalent |
| `FetchingTree.File` cat-file fallback | ✅ benefits both (it's checkpoint-package-level) | ✅ also benefits v2 (any v2 path that uses FetchingTree gets the speedup) |
| `FetchBlobs` switched to fetch-pack | ✅ benefits both | ✅ benefits both |

**Practical impact for your case:** your settings have `preferCheckpointsV2: false`, so this is a non-issue today — the read path goes straight to v1, which is fully fixed.

**If v2 gets enabled later:** if a checkpoint lives in v2 with locally-missing blobs, my fixes cover the discovery side (the empty-matches fetch finds it) but **not** the blob-read side. `V2GitStore.ReadCommitted` would still hit the original go-git `ErrFileNotFound`-on-missing-blob behavior, which the resolver translates to `ErrCheckpointNotFound` — the exact same false-negative bug we just fixed for v1.

**The fix for v2 would mirror v1:**
1. Add `SetBlobFetcher` + `blobFetcher` field on `V2GitStore` (parallel to `GitStore.SetBlobFetcher`)
2. Wire it into V2GitStore's `getFetchingTree` equivalent (wherever it constructs the FetchingTree it reads from)
3. Add a `prefetchCheckpointBlobsV2` that uses `getV2MetadataTree` to navigate to the v2 cp subtree

I deliberately didn't do this in the current commit because:
- v2 is off by default and not relevant to your bug report
- It would roughly double the change size and require V2GitStore API changes
- It deserves its own commit/PR with v2-specific testing

Want me to do the v2 mirror as a follow-up commit on the same branch, or leave it as a known gap? If you want the gap documented, I can add a brief comment in `newExplainCheckpointLookup` or open a TODO somewhere.

573		}

794	// TestExplain_CheckpointSucceedsAfterTreelessFetch covers the partial-clone
795	// scenario the original bug surfaced in: a collaborator does a treeless
796	// fetch (--filter=blob:none) of the metadata branch. Tree entries land
797	// locally so ListCommitted can find the checkpoint, but the metadata.json
798	// blob is absent from go-git's view. Without the blob fetcher + cat-file
799	// fallback, ReadCommitted returned (nil, nil) which the resolver translated
800	// to "checkpoint not found" — even though the checkpoint genuinely exists.
801	//
802	// Regression test for: explain failing with "no checkpoint or commit found"
803	// against a checkpoint_remote-style setup with filtered_fetches enabled.
804	func TestExplain_CheckpointSucceedsAfterTreelessFetch(t *testing.T) {
805		t.Parallel()
806		env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
807	
808		bareRemoteURL := env.SetupBareRemote()
809	
810		session := env.NewSession()
811		transcriptPath := session.CreateTranscript("Treeless v1 prompt", []FileChange{
812			{Path: "treeless_v1.go", Content: "package treeless"},
813		})
814		require.NoError(t, env.SimulateUserPromptSubmitWithPromptAndTranscriptPath(session.ID, "Treeless v1 prompt", transcriptPath))
815		env.WriteFile("treeless_v1.go", "package treeless")
816		env.GitAdd("treeless_v1.go")
817		require.NoError(t, env.SimulateStop(session.ID, transcriptPath))
818		env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add treeless v1 feature", "treeless_v1.go")
819	
820		checkpointID := env.GetLatestCheckpointID()
821		require.NotEmpty(t, checkpointID, "expected a checkpoint after condensation")
822	
823		env.RunPrePush("origin")
824	
825		// Wipe local v1 metadata refs and re-fetch with --filter=blob:none.
826		// This leaves trees locally but no blobs — the exact partial-clone state
827		// that reproduced the original bug.
828		repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
829		require.NoError(t, err)
830		_ = repo.Storer.RemoveReference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName))
831		_ = repo.Storer.RemoveReference(plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName("origin", paths.MetadataBranchName))
832	
833		refspec := "+refs/heads/" + paths.MetadataBranchName + ":refs/heads/" + paths.MetadataBranchName
834		cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "git", "fetch", "--filter=blob:none", "--depth=1", "--no-tags", bareRemoteURL, refspec)
835		cmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
836		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
837		if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
838			t.Fatalf("treeless fetch failed: %v\n%s", err, out)
839		}
840	
841		// Sanity-check: verify the local branch tip is set but at least one
842		// metadata.json blob is genuinely missing from the local store. Without
843		// this assertion the test would silently pass even if the treeless fetch
844		// somehow grabbed blobs.
845		_, err = repo.Storer.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName))
846		require.NoError(t, err, "treeless fetch should have set the local metadata branch")
847		requireSomeMetadataBlobMissing(t, env.RepoDir, checkpointID)

849		output := env.RunCLI("explain", "--checkpoint", checkpointID)

851			"explain should succeed and surface the prompt despite blobs being absent locally")

915	// requireSomeMetadataBlobMissing fails the test if every blob entry in the
916	// checkpoint's v1 metadata subtree is locally accessible. Used to verify a
917	// treeless fetch genuinely produced a blob-missing state before exercising
918	// the read path.
919	func requireSomeMetadataBlobMissing(t *testing.T, repoDir, checkpointID string) {
920		t.Helper()
921		repo, err := git.PlainOpen(repoDir)
922		require.NoError(t, err)
923		ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
924		require.NoError(t, err)
925		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
926		require.NoError(t, err)
927		rootTree, err := commit.Tree()
928		require.NoError(t, err)
929		cpSubtree, err := rootTree.Tree(checkpointID[:2] + "/" + checkpointID[2:])
930		require.NoError(t, err)
931	
932		if _, err := cpSubtree.File(paths.MetadataFileName); err != nil {
933			// File entry not visible at all — counts as "missing".
934			return
935		}
936		// File entry exists; check whether the blob is actually loadable. After
937		// --filter=blob:none, FindEntry succeeds but Contents() should fail
938		// (ErrFileNotFound surfaces from missing-blob lookups in go-git).
939		for _, entry := range cpSubtree.Entries {
940			if !entry.Mode.IsFile() {

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(cli): mirror partial-clone explain fix for v2 + add regression tests

The v1 fix in 645fb1252 left v2 vulnerable to the same bug: when a
metadata blob is on the remote but absent locally, V2GitStore's read
path used raw `*object.Tree.File()` calls which return ErrFileNotFound
on missing blobs — and ReadCommitted treats that as "checkpoint not
found". This blocks `entire explain` against partial-clone repos as
soon as checkpoints_v2 is enabled.

v2 fix mirrors v1:
- V2GitStore gains `blobFetcher` + `SetBlobFetcher` (parallel to GitStore).
- ReadCommitted, ReadSessionCompactTranscript, ReadSessionMetadataAndPrompts,
  and ReadSessionContent now wrap their cp/session subtrees in
  FetchingTree before calling File(). FetchingTree's cat-file fallback
  + on-demand fetcher recover blobs that go-git's storer can't see.
- explain configures FetchBlobsByHash on both v1 and v2 stores.
- prefetchCheckpointBlobs walks both v1 and v2 cp subtrees so a single
  fetch-pack round-trip primes both stores.

Regression tests in cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/explain_test.go:
- TestExplain_CheckpointSucceedsAfterTreelessFetch (v1)
- TestExplain_CheckpointV2SucceedsAfterTreelessFetch (v2)

Both reproduce the bug-triggering state by:
1. Pushing a checkpoint to a bare remote.
2. Cloning into a fresh TempDir with `--filter=blob:none --depth=1` over
   `file://` URL (uploadpack.allowFilter set on the bare). This gives
   the clone tree entries but no blobs — the actual partial-clone state.
3. Asserting at least one metadata blob is genuinely missing (otherwise
   the test would silently pass without exercising the fix).
4. Running explain in the clone and verifying the prompt text is in the
   output.

Verified: stashing the v2 fix and running TestExplain_CheckpointV2SucceedsAfterTreelessFetch
fails with `failed to read checkpoint: checkpoint not found` — the
exact original bug — confirming the test catches regressions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
